headline: Voted 9-0 to proceed with Catherine Foster as budget analyst, Gary Frisch as second choice, pending HR checks.
summary: Councilors interviewed Gary Frisch and Katherine Foster for the budget/management analyst job. Several councilors said they favored Foster, citing her municipal finance experience and her research on Beverly. The current analyst offered to stay on through the transition.

transcript:
Received and recorded by City Clerk: 2026 NOV 19

# City of Beverly
## Special City Council Meeting
## Public Meeting Minutes
## Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6:00 PM
## First Floor Conference Room, 175 Cabot Street

Julie Flowers, City Council President, called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. President Flowers took attendance by roll call.

Members Present: Julie Flowers, Matthew St. Hilaire, Steven Crowley, Scott Houseman, John Mullady, Todd Rotondo, Keith Sonia, Danielle Spang. Kathleen Feldman joined the meeting at 6:36 PM

Members Absent: None

Also Present: City Solicitor Beth Oldmixon, Budget/Management Analyst Gerry Perry.

### Budget/Management Analyst Candidate Interviews:

#### 6:00 PM-Gary Frisch

Gary Frisch joined the meeting at 6:01 PM. He introduced himself as a school business official with more than 25 years of experience, preceded by approximately nine years as an assistant school business official.

Crowley asked about the most important role of the Budget Analyst. Mr. Frisch described analyzing the budget, developing recommendations, and helping guide the Council to determine allocations that best serve residents, schools, and municipal departments. He emphasized his experience with school finances, noting that schools represent approximately half of the City budget.

Mullady asked about Mr. Frisch's knowledge of Beverly's current financial status. Mr. Frisch referenced increases in trash contractor costs and the resulting trash fee controversy. He anticipated pressure from health insurance, special education, and contractor costs and said that reducing school expenditures to balance the budget would be difficult. He emphasized evaluating the needs of both school and municipal services.

Sonia asked Mr. Frisch would approach working with councilors from different backgrounds. Mr. Frisch said he would start with foundational information, build toward more complex material, and be patient with questions.

St. Hilaire asked what challenges Mr. Frisch anticipated in transitioning into the role. Mr. Frisch said he was fully familiar with school operations and had experience with city processes, including work in Gloucester. He would meet with Beverly's finance director to learn City-specific procedures and responsibilities.

President Flowers noted the upcoming departure of Beverly's Finance Director and asked how Mr. Frish would advise the Council through periods of transition. Mr. Frisch said he would work patiently with new councilors and establish mutual understanding. Regarding staff turnover, he emphasized hiring qualified personnel, providing thorough training, and helping new employees become comfortable in their roles.

Houseman asked whether his school-focused experience would be an advantage or handicap in evaluating school and municipal priorities. Mr. Frisch considered it an advantage, saying it could close gaps in understanding between school and City operations. He stressed communication before the administration finalizes a budget, reciprocal sharing of information, and recommendations based on the needs of the entire community rather than favoring either side.

Crowley asked how he would maintain independence and objectivity when analysis disagrees with the administration or a department. Mr. Frisch emphasized understanding both perspectives and examining the information to reach a better-informed conclusion.

Mullady asked Mr. Frisch's familiarity with Proposition 2½. Mr. Frisch discussed the limit on annual property tax levy increases, the addition of new growth, and the distinction between communities taking the full allowable increase and those below their levy limit.

Sonia asked how he would respond to councilors with differing priorities and opinions. Mr. Frisch described budgeting as both an art and a science, requiring consideration of competing interests while focusing on facts rather than opinions.

St. Hilaire asked about responding to a difficult financial situation. Mr. Frisch discussed Beverly's deficit reduction efforts and suggested examining health insurance costs with bargaining units participating in discussions. He said the City should identify the size of the deficit, establish a reduction target, and evaluate possible savings while recognizing revenue limits under Proposition 2½.

President Flowers asked about reporting to a multi-member body. Mr. Frisch described his work with a school finance and building committee, where he built trust by explaining the facts and walking members through recommendations.

Rotondo asked how he would navigate the loss of institutional knowledge amid departures in finance positions. Mr. Frisch said he would learn from the current Budget Analyst and departing finance director before their departures and draw on contacts from prior municipal work.

Houseman followed up on health insurance and collective bargaining. Mr. Frisch suggested that someone representing the Council, potentially the Budget Analyst, participate in relevant insurance discussions and report back so councilors would understand the issues before any decisions.

Feldman joined the meeting at 6:36 PM

Sonia asked how proactively he would bring ideas to the Council. Mr. Frisch said he continually looks for savings opportunities that could address deficits or support additional programs and services.

St. Hilaire asked why he wanted the position. Mr. Frisch said he enjoyed sharing his knowledge and bringing forward ideas for constructive change and saw an opportunity to make a difference.

President Flowers asked about his availability. Mr. Frisch said he was generally available, apart from a standing personal training commitment on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2:00 to 3:00 p.m.

Spang asked about Mr. Frisch's experience with Munis. Mr. Frisch said he had ten years of experience using it for budget reports and budget development.

Rotondo asked about Mr. Frisch's anticipated strengths and challenges transitioning into the role. Mr. Frisch identified budget forecasting as a particular strength, especially with the financial forecasting committee's report approaching. He said he would need to learn certain municipal policies and procedures but would plan to use the current analyst and Department of Revenue website as resources.

Houseman asked how Mr. Frisch would handle strong personalities when there was disagreement. Mr. Frisch explained that he would lay out the facts and, if necessary, agree to disagree. His role was to help the Council reach a decision, not to win an argument.

Mr. Frisch asked when the position would begin and whether humor was welcome in the Council's working environment. President Flowers and Rotondo described a collegial atmosphere with humor and mutual respect, including during disagreements. President Flowers explained that Mr. Perry had offered to remain through the end of the calendar year or the financial forecast process to help transition his responsibilities. The Council hoped a new analyst could begin soon enough to allow for a handoff.

A motion to recess was made and seconded. A vote was taken, and motion carried (9-0). The meeting recessed from 6:53 PM until 7:00 PM when President Flowers called the meeting back to order.

#### 7:00 PM-Katherine Foster

Katherine Foster joined the meeting at 7:00 PM. Ms. Foster described her experience in municipal government, management analysis, and data analysis. She explained that she had moved into the private sector for personal reasons but remained interested in contributing to municipal government.

Crowley asked about the Budget Analyst's most important responsibility. Ms. Foster described the role as an independent check and balance for the Council while maintaining productive relationships with municipal staff. She would perform independent analysis, compare findings with the finance director's work, identify potential issues and alternatives early, and communicate disagreements professionally.

Feldman asked about Ms. Foster's knowledge of Beverly's current financial condition and management practices. Ms. Foster said she had reviewed a June budget meeting and recognized the difficulty of balancing the budget through reductions. She identified pressures involving education and vocational education, state aid, Proposition 2½, capital equipment costs, collective bargaining, employee retention, health insurance, other post-employment benefits, and trash costs. On financial practices, she emphasized transparent analysis, salary comparisons, management reviews, health insurance and workers' compensation analysis, and enterprise fund rate-setting based on data.

Sonia asked how Ms. Foster would assist councilors with different finance background. Ms. Foster said she would guide them through questions and financial information, using state resources as appropriate. She described explaining budgets to new department heads and elected officials and in the private sector helping individuals understand financial decisions. Her experience with departments would also help her explain competing needs.

Sonia excused himself from the meeting at 7:11 PM.

St. Hilaire asked about moving from an administrative advisory role to advising the Council. Ms. Foster acknowledged the challenge of working with councilors who do not handle departmental operations daily. She said the role would involve bridging that gap, working cooperatively with City staff, and helping the Council understand details that cannot all be covered in budget presentations.

President Flowers discussed the pending departure of the City finance director and asked about working through transitions in staffing and elected leadership. Ms. Foster described a previous period when she served in several roles, including treasurer-collector, finance director, and assistant town manager, during substantial turnover. She said she sought Department of Revenue guidance on restructuring and relied on collaboration, patience, education, and multiple options when circumstances changed.

Crowley asked how she would maintain independence if her recommendation differed from the administration or department. Ms. Foster said she would first discuss the assumptions and circumstances with the finance director and appropriate staff, then present her own conclusion respectfully if differences remained. She emphasized the importance of the analyst serving as independent eyes for the Council.

Feldman asked for a plain-language explanation of Proposition 2½. Ms. Foster described the tax recap as a snapshot of how the levy and tax rate are calculated, including the 2½ percent increase, new growth, state aid, local receipts, and other resources used to balance the budget.

St. Hilaire asked about a difficult financial challenge. Ms. Foster described her work in Dracut during an approximately $8 million deficit, when the town had approximately $11 million in certified free cash. She explained that options included using free cash, implementing a trash fee, or eliminating trash service. She supported the trash fee while acknowledging that it was unpopular and did not resolve the underlying structural deficit. She discussed concerns about meeting net school spending, potential future override discussions, and the need for early and frequent public communication about trade-offs and essential services.

President Flowers asked about reporting to a multi-member body. Ms. Foster described her experience with capital expenditure, finance, and appropriations committees. She said she would learn individual members' preferred ways of receiving information, including written memoranda, visual data, or telephone discussions, while building relationships with members and the body as a whole.

Rotondo asked about preserving institutional knowledge as finance personnel depart. Ms. Foster said she would meet with current and departing employees, review documented policies and procedures, consult remaining staff and appropriate boards and committees, and use state agencies and professional associations as resources.

Spang asked Ms. Fosters about her experience with financial software. Ms. Foster said she had used Munis and Vadar, primarily Munis, for payroll data, general ledger reports, balances, and year-over-year comparisons. She preferred Munis for its reporting capabilities.

Houseman asked how she could help councilors explain difficult financial decisions to residents. Ms. Foster described a Citizens Academy, later called Civic Academy, in a previous community. She said the approximately 11-week program brought residents together with department heads to learn about budgets, facilities, services, Proposition 2½, and proposed capital projects. She also suggested accessible communications through newsletters, a public information officer, budget conversations or coffee hour.

St. Hilaire asked what interested her in the position. Ms. Foster said she had moved to a private-sector financial analyst role to obtain more flexibility and balance while raising two young children, but remained passionate about municipal government and financial analysis. She hoped the Council position would allow her to continue work in a field in which she had invested considerable education and experience, while maintaining a more manageable schedule. She acknowledged that the position would involve evening meetings.

President Flowers asked how Ms. Foster would remain accessible while balancing employment and family. Ms. Foster anticipated calls and meetings, including calls while traveling or arranged after family commitments. She said she wanted the role because of her continuing passion for municipal work and desire to support the Council, City staff, and community.

Rotondo asked about the challenges and strengths Ms. Foster anticipated during her first six months. Ms. Foster identified the finance director's departure and the need to learn Beverly's budget quickly during budget preparation as significant challenges. She said her experience working through turnover, taking on new municipal responsibilities, and meeting legal requirements would help her adapt.

Houseman followed up on her availability, confirming that her private-sector position was primarily remote and allowed some flexibility during the workday to take calls. Ms. Foster confirmed.

Ms. Foster asked about the expected hiring timeline and challenges associated with the finance director's departure. President Flowers said current Budget Analyst Jerry Perry had offered to remain through the financial forecasting process to transfer institutional knowledge and facilitate a smooth transition. She said the Council hoped to fill the position sooner rather than later. Rotondo emphasized that the analyst would advise the Council, rather than be responsible for filling vacant City positions or solving all municipal financial problems. Councilor Feldman described the financial forecasting process as an immediate learning opportunity, with work in November and a report due by the end of the year, followed by preparation for the budget season. President Flowers agreed that the new analyst's responsibility would be to advise the Council through the transition and noted the challenge of rebuilding relationships and trust following the departure of experienced City personnel.

Houseman asked how Ms. Foster would approach people with strong personalities. Ms. Foster said she would begin by listening, recognizing that people often want to be heard, and then respectfully explain her position. If disagreement continued, she would continue to emphasize listening and education rather than expect agreement in every case.

Ms. Foster asked whether financial forecasting had begun. Houseman explained that meetings would be scheduled once school financial figures were received and anticipated approximately three meetings in November. Ms. Foster thanked the Council for the interview and the opportunity to learn about the position. The Council thanked her for attending.

A motion to recess was made and seconded. A vote was taken, and motion carried (9-0). The meeting recessed from 7:54 PM until 8:00 PM when President Flowers called the meeting back to order.

### Discussion of Candidates for Consideration for Hiring for the City Council Budget Management Analyst Position

President Flowers noted that Mr. Perry was present to clarify the role and responsibilities but would not recommend a candidate. Councilors indicated readiness to proceed, and she invited their preferences and reasons.

Rotondo favored Catherine Foster for her municipal finance experience, confidence, understanding of the role, and readiness amid staffing changes.

Spang also favored Ms. Foster for her compensation studies and demeanor.

Crowley also favored Ms. Foster, echoing previous councilor statements and noting her presentation and understanding of the role.

Mullady indicated he was between Mr. Frisch and Ms. Foster. He appreciated Mr. Frisch's experience with the school department, and his answered geared towards importance of different needs and sharing information, to say Ms. Foster did not.

Feldman noted that she was not present for most of Mr. Frisch's interview, she thought his answers were good but favored Ms. Foster due to her experience and understanding based on her own research.

St. Hilaire noted he appreciated Mr. Frisch's strong mayor government views and noted Ms. Foster's experience but expressed concern about Ms. Foster's ability to devote the necessary hours to the position while maintaining full-time employment

Housman noted Mr. Frisch experience in a city vs town over Ms. Foster, but each had their own unique experience to draw from. Housman also recognized the research Ms. Foster conducted on the city.

Councilor voiced concerns over Ms. Foster's availability in her stage and life and working a full time job.

The City Solicitor clarified that restrictions on working for two municipalities were not an absolute prohibition and did not apply to her situation. She reminded members that Ms. Foster had affirmed she could manage both roles. Some councilors remained concerned about peak-season availability.

Mr. Perry responded to questions about the workload. He stated that he had worked approximately 600 hours annually, while his predecessor had worked more than 800, and that hours depended partly on the individual's approach. He described busy forecasting work from September through December, a quieter January and February, increasing work especially in May and June for budget hearings. Summer was substantially quieter.

Sonia returned to the meeting at 8:16 PM.

Houseman asked whether the Council could seek additional clarification from Ms. Foster about her availability during the busiest budget months. Spang and Rotondo noted that the screening committee had already explained the seasonal workload and that she had confirmed her ability to meet those demands. Houseman also asked whether Mr. Perry had identified technical errors or strengths in either candidate's interview answers. President Flowers and Councilors expressed concern that such an assessment would come too close to asking Mr. Perry to evaluate or rank candidates. Houseman said Mr. Frisch's answer regarding collective bargaining had raised a technical concern for him.

Sonia favored Ms. Foster praising her public communication, preparation, and experience, while recognizing the qualifications of Mr. Frisch and another previously interviewed candidate, Frederique Pierre-Lyne Phanor.

Rotondo suggested that virtual or hybrid meetings could reduce travel demands and noted that Mr. Perry's continued service during the transition would help preserve institutional knowledge. He believed Ms. Foster would have the easier transition given her municipal finance background.

St Hilaire noted Ms. Foster had been well prepared but expressed a different view of Mr. Frisch's municipal budget strengths and reiterated that he would be comfortable with either candidate if the Council was satisfied with their ability to meet the position's needs.

### Potential Vote to elect a candidate for the Position of Budget/ Management Analyst

Rotondo moved to proceed with Catherine Foster as the first candidate, contingent upon completion of all required HR procedures, including review of references and other applicable requirements, and to proceed with Gary Frisch as the second candidate under the same conditions if the first appointment did not go forward. The motion was seconded.

Before the vote, President Flowers temporarily yielded the chair to Vice President St. Hilaire so she could share her assessment. She said she would be comfortable with either candidate but considered Ms. Foster the stronger candidate, particularly because she heard and answered the questions councilors were actually asking. She also cited Ms. Foster's research into Beverly's budget process, prior meetings, and use of ClearGov, while recognizing Mr. Frisch's steady experience. President Flowers thanked the screening committee and the Council for the discussion.

A vote was taken, and motion carried (9-0).

Mr. Perry offered to help transfer institutional knowledge, reports, and guidance through forecasting. Councilors expressed support for a transition period and discussed how Mr. Perry's files and experience could be made available to the incoming analyst.

Councilors asked whether HR could contact other applicants about additional City vacancies. The City Solicitor indicated that this was generally part of the City's hiring practice. She described the appointment process, which includes reference checks, a CORI check, drug screening, and verification of eligibility to work, while noting there could be other requirements.

It was discussed to provide a verbal offer followed by a written offer contingent on onboarding and agreed not to offer the position to the second candidate unless the first process concluded without an appointment.

A motion to adjourn was made and seconded. A vote was taken, and motion carried (9-0). The meeting adjourned at 8:56 PM.
